1. Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or volatile.  
2. When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0), model should reduce forecasted price by 5-10% relative to recent highs.  
3. If last 3-5 days show strong upward momentum, model should not over-forecast beyond 10% above recent peak.  
4. Mean reversion is strong in 10-14 day horizons — model should adjust downward if true outcome shows >15% deviation from 10-day moving average.  
5. Overshoot after sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.5+ in sentiment) often leads to 3-5 day correction — model should cap forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment > +1.0.  
6. When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model should apply a downward bias of 2-5% per day to avoid overcorrection.  
7. Model underestimates in low-sentiment periods — if sentiment < -0.5 for 3+ days, add 3-5% to forecast to account for hidden demand or policy effects.
